There is already a well though out system that is hardly used. Digital signatures to verify an identity is what PGP does. It does it well. It already exist, and has more options than merely proving someone had bitcoins at some date and time. The blockchain along only proves approximate time. This hardly identifies someone, only sometime. It's hardly and identification service, only a timestamp.

However PGP can verify identity. Someone you know, can make a verifiable statement, that someone else exist. With enough verifiable statements, an identity can assumed to be accurate. It matter much less when the statement was made, more credible is who said it.

I am in principle in favour these ideas but an eventual problem comes to my mind - the lack of control.
